verdict.rationale: PagerDuty's own Shift Agent documentation says it detects conflicts, identifies qualified replacements, and coordinates schedule changes without manual intervention, which covers requesting coverage without an admin. Community reports confirm overrides and rotation trades exist but describe them as clunky and manual ("overrides on top of overrides"), which is an ergonomics complaint rather than a concrete contradiction. missing for 10: first-party docs on engineer self-service overrides and shift swaps, documented permission model showing no admin is needed, detail on the mobile schedules feature, independent corroboration that the Shift Agent works.

support.subject: As an on-call engineer, I can take an override, swap a shift, or request coverage without an admin rebuilding the schedule

citations.quote: monitors calendars, detects potential conflicts, identifies qualified replacements, and coordinates schedule changes without manual intervention
Taking a week of vacation meant heavy manual schedule adjustment, "overrides on top of overrides", and negotiating rotation trades with teammates.
